output.body:
# Discovery, finding whether a facility holds records

## In plain words

The step where a patient's [PHR](phr.md) app asks a facility whether it
holds records for that patient. The [HIE-CM](hie-cm.md) forwards the
request to the [HIP](hip.md) with verified identifiers (ABHA address,
mobile number, name, gender, year of birth) and any unverified
identifier the patient typed, such as a hospital patient ID. Your system
matches those against your own patients and replies with a list of [care
contexts](/docs/hiecm/v3/concepts/care-context), carrying no clinical detail.

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say what discovery returns when a facility holds nothing for that patient.

## When it goes wrong

Treating a discovery hit as permission to send data. Discovery only says
records exist. Sending them still needs a linked care context and a
granted consent.

reply.Text:
**Discovery in ABDM** is the step where a patient's PHR app asks a facility whether it holds records for that patient.

Here's how it works:

- The patient initiates discovery from their PHR app
- HIE-CM forwards the request to the health information provider (HIP) with:
  - Verified identifiers: ABHA address, mobile number, name, gender, year of birth
  - Any unverified identifiers the patient entered (like a hospital patient ID)
- Your facility matches those identifiers against your patient records
- You respond with a list of **care contexts** the patient has at your facility—but **without any clinical detail**

**Key point:** Discovery only tells you that records exist. It's not permission to send data. To actually send records, you still need:
- A linked care context
- A granted consent from the patient

See the HIE-CM glossary on the [developer portal](https://developer.abdm.gov.in/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#discovery).
